english.note: Use this as the everyday Hong Kong Cantonese noun for a beautiful woman or girl.

exampleSentences.english: That beauty drinks coffee at the café downstairs every day.
exampleSentences.traditional: 嗰個靚女日日都喺樓下間咖啡店飲咖啡。
exampleSentences.jyutping: go2 go3 leng3 neoi5 jat6 jat6 dou1 hai2 lau4 haa6 gaan1 gaa3 fe1 dim3 jam2 gaa3 fe1

english.note: Use this for the slang sense of an attractive young woman, rather than for a literal toy.

exampleSentences.english: That doll walked in, and everyone stared at her.
exampleSentences.traditional: 嗰個靚女一入場，成班人都望住佢。
exampleSentences.jyutping: go2 go3 leng3 neoi5 jat1 jap6 coeng4 sing4 baan1 jan4 dou1 mong6 zyu6 keoi5

english.note: Use 靚女 when referring casually to an attractive woman rather than addressing someone affectionately.

exampleSentences.english: That honey reads at the café every day.
exampleSentences.traditional: 嗰個靚女成日喺咖啡店睇書。
exampleSentences.jyutping: go2 go3 leng3 neoi5 sing4 jat6 hai2 gaa3 fe1 dim3 tai2 syu1

english.note: Use this when angel means a beautiful girl, woman, or young person, especially in casual Hong Kong speech.

exampleSentences.english: That beautiful girl has such a sweet smile; she’s an angel.
exampleSentences.jyutping: go2 go3 leng3 neoi5 siu3 dak1 hou2 tim4

english.note: Use this when “bird” refers specifically to an attractive girl or woman.

exampleSentences.english: When that attractive bird walked in, all the guys stared at her.
exampleSentences.traditional: 嗰個靚女一入場，成班男仔都望住佢。
exampleSentences.jyutping: go2 go3 leng3 neoi5 jat1 jap6 coeng4 seng4 baan1 naam4 zai2 dou1 mong6 zyu6 keoi5
